Toppling Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs

Originally published

WritingIf you need a refresher on Maslow’s pyramid, it’s got five levels: 5. Self Actualization Skill- and value-based concerns like morality, creativity, problem solving, acceptance of facts, etc. 4. Self-esteem Individual achievements, mutual respect, which inoculate our self-confidence and boost our morale. 3. Love & Belonging Emotional support, affection, and social recognition, which keep us happy, calm and saner. 2. Safety Security in our selves, jobs, resources, family, property, assets, etc. 1. Physiology Basic existential requirements like food, clothing and shelter. Of utmost importance. In reality: the pyramid levels are much less distinct Individual achievements are often skill- and value-based. Feeling secure in our “jobs” (AKA primary income-earning method) is inexorably tied to our physiological needs because, in a culture based on economic growth & currency, we are focused on earning income to pay for our needs rather than bringing our most valuable contributions to the world. Regrouping Maslow’s pyramid levels I propose the following structure: Self Actualization Addresses larger self esteem themes Work: Careers/vocations Love: Self-love Belonging & Mental Health Love: Family, friends groups, communities, “tribes” Work: The myriad activities & contributions required to keep a community going. Addresses part of self esteem. Technically this blends in below Physical Survival Basic physiological needs Food, water, air, clothing & shelter, sex, sleep, excretion Resources to survive, like weapons (not in security) What’s getting in the way of… Physiological needs? Abundance of resources aren’t efficiently distributed (capitalism/profit-based problem) Material security? Cost of living has gotten too high (capitalism/profit-based problem) Most accessible jobs don’t or can’t pay “a living wage” (education problem) Love & belonging? People don’t know how to build conscious relationships very effectively (p2p relationship problem) People aren’t hearing about local communities (b2c distribution problem) Esteem? ??? bullying / lack of social support? Is this actually part of love & belonging? Self-actualization? People don’t know how to go from “work that pays the bills” to “work that fulfills me” (education & network problem) • • •View full archive ↗

Originally published

If you need a refresher on Maslow’s pyramid, it’s got five levels:

5. Self Actualization

Skill- and value-based concerns like morality, creativity, problem solving, acceptance of facts, etc.

4. Self-esteem

Individual achievements, mutual respect, which inoculate our self-confidence and boost our morale.

3. Love & Belonging

Emotional support, affection, and social recognition, which keep us happy, calm and saner.

2. Safety

Security in our selves, jobs, resources, family, property, assets, etc.

1. Physiology

Basic existential requirements like food, clothing and shelter. Of utmost importance.

In reality: the pyramid levels are much less distinct

Individual achievements are often skill- and value-based. Feeling secure in our “jobs” (AKA primary income-earning method) is inexorably tied to our physiological needs because, in a culture based on economic growth & currency, we are focused on earning income to pay for our needs rather than bringing our most valuable contributions to the world.

Regrouping Maslow’s pyramid levels

I propose the following structure:

Self Actualization

Addresses larger self esteem themes

Work: Careers/vocations

Love: Self-love

Belonging & Mental Health

Love: Family, friends groups, communities, “tribes” 

Work: The myriad activities & contributions required to keep a community going. Addresses part of self esteem. Technically this blends in below

Physical Survival

Basic physiological needs

Food, water, air, clothing & shelter, sex, sleep, excretion

Resources to survive, like weapons (not in security)

What’s getting in the way of…

Physiological needs?

Abundance of resources aren’t efficiently distributed (capitalism/profit-based problem)

Material security?

Cost of living has gotten too high (capitalism/profit-based problem)

Most accessible jobs don’t or can’t pay “a living wage” (education problem)

Love & belonging?

People don’t know how to build conscious relationships very effectively (p2p relationship problem)

People aren’t hearing about local communities (b2c distribution problem)

Esteem?

??? bullying / lack of social support? Is this actually part of love & belonging?

Self-actualization?

People don’t know how to go from “work that pays the bills” to “work that fulfills me” (education & network problem)
